Starting at $599, the MacBook Neo outclasses Windows rivals like the HP OmniBook 3 and OmniBook 5. Even though the OmniBook 5 costs $100 more, Apple delivers stronger hardware, speed, and screen sharpness. Build quality is where the MacBook Neo really shines, and it's tough to beat. Apple uses a rigid, 60 percent recycled aluminum unibody shell in four colors that weighs 2.7 pounds. Reviewers at Notebookcheck and PCMag praise its sturdy frame and lack of keyboard flex. Its Multi-Touch trackpad also gives you accurate cursor control that rival Windows touchpads rarely match. By contrast, the HP OmniBook 3 relies on plastic keycaps and feels bulkier in larger chassis sizes. Inside, iFixit named the Neo the most repairable MacBook in 14 years, citing modular ports and screw-mounted batteries. Performance also favors Apple silicon in everyday use. The MacBook Neo runs the A18 Pro chip with a 6-core CPU, 5-core GPU, and 16-core Neural Engine. PCMag measured faster daily speeds and graphics than rival laptops in its price class. Meanwhile, the base HP OmniBook 5 uses an Intel Core 5 320 with weak integrated graphics. PCWorld tests showed it scoring just 1,655 in Time Spy. ZDNET also notes that 8GB of unified memory goes further in macOS than 8GB in Windows 11. Plus, it doesn't need cooling fans, so it runs silently. Display sharpness gives Apple another big win. The Neo packs a 13-inch Liquid Retina screen with 2408 by 1506 resolution and 500 nits brightness. That 219 pixels-per-inch density keeps text crisp and supports Dolby Vision and HDR10+ video. While the HP OmniBook 5 uses a 14-inch OLED panel, it drops to 1920 by 1200 resolution. Its 300-nit peak brightness and glossy finish also cause glare in bright rooms, according to ZDNET. PCMag found the Neo screen brighter and sharper than almost any rival at this price. Everyday extras widen the gap even more. The Neo includes dual speakers with Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos, whereas ZDNET faulted the OmniBook 5's speakers. BGR also points out that macOS links with iPhone Mirroring, AirDrop, and instant AirPods switching.
